At Körber Supply Chain DK, we design and deliver advanced automated material handling solutions to customers worldwide. As demand continues to grow and our project portfolio expands, we are looking for an experienced Lead Mechanical Engineer to strengthen our Mechanical Engineering team in Arden.

This is a key technical leadership role where you will take ownership of the mechanical engineering discipline across complex automation projects. You will play a central role in ensuring high-quality engineering solutions while driving collaboration across projects, teams, and stakeholders.

Your role:

As Lead Mechanical Engineer, you will be responsible for leading and coordinating all mechanical engineering activities throughout the project lifecycle, from concept development and design through manufacturing, installation, and commissioning.

You will act as the technical lead within the mechanical discipline, ensuring that solutions meet customer requirements, comply with relevant standards, and are delivered on time and with the expected level of quality.

Working closely with Project Managers, Electrical and Software Engineers, customers, suppliers, and external partners, you will help turn complex requirements into practical and reliable automation solutions.

Your responsibilities will include:

•    Leading and coordinating mechanical engineering activities across projects

•    Developing and reviewing mechanical concepts, layouts, and detailed designs•    Ensuring compliance with machinery directives, safety standards, and internal engineering guidelines

•    Managing and supporting internal engineers and external engineering resources

•    Conducting design reviews, technical evaluations, and risk assessments

•    Providing technical leadership and mentoring within the Mechanical Engineering team

•    Supporting procurement activities through technical specifications and supplier evaluations

•    Ensuring timely delivery of engineering documentation, including drawings, BOMs, calculations, and technical reports

•    Supporting manufacturing, installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting activities when required

Your profile:

You are an experienced mechanical engineer who combines strong technical expertise with natural leadership skills. You enjoy taking ownership, setting direction, and supporting colleagues while remaining hands-on when needed. Proven ability to lead multiple projects simultaneously across different stages, from design and procurement through manufacturing and installation. You maintain a forward-looking overview of priorities, dependencies and resource requirements, ensuring a balanced workload and early communication of potential capacity constraints or deadline impacts.

You are comfortable working in a project-driven environment where priorities may change and where collaboration across disciplines and cultures is key to success.

We imagine that you have:

You hold a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Technology, or a related technical discipline and bring 7-10 years of experience within mechanical design and development of customer-specific machinery or automation solutions. You have a proven track record as a Lead Engineer or technical lead on complex engineering projects and possess strong experience with 3D CAD systems such as Autodesk Inventor, SolidWorks, or similar tools.

In addition, you have a solid understanding of mechanical design principles, manufacturing processes, material selection, and tolerancing, combined with experience in stakeholder management and cross-functional project collaboration. Knowledge of machine safety, CE marking, risk assessments, and relevant industry standards is expected. Finally, you are a strong communicator with excellent written and spoken English skills. Experience within material handling, intralogistics, automation systems, ERP/PLM systems, or delivery of machinery to the North American market will be considered an advantage.

Why Should You Join Körber Supply Chain DK?

We offer an exciting role in an international company in growth, where you will work with advanced technical solutions and be part of a strong professional environment characterized by collaboration and dedication. We offer a range of attractive employee benefits:

Security & Health: In addition to a competitive salary package, you will be enrolled in our mandatory pension scheme, which also includes both health insurance and dental insurance, as well as access to physiotherapy. You will also be part of our lunch program, where our canteen provides healthy and exciting meals every day.

Development: We continuously offer training and courses, as we believe that our success is built on satisfied and skilled employees. That’s why we focus on both personal and professional development to ensure continuous growth.

Social Events: We have a strong company culture that we invest heavily in maintaining and developing. This includes a wide range of events and an active employee association that organizes activities such as Friday bars, Christmas parties, an annual ski trip, cultural events, and much more!

Körber – Conquer Supply Chain Complexity

We value diversity and welcome all applicants, regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion/belief, disability, age, sexual orientation, identity, or any other protected status.

**Apply now:**If you would like to create your future as a part of the Körber Supply Chain DK A/S team, please forward your application and CV already today!

Applications for this position have no deadline, as we will include candidates in the recruitment process on a continuous basis and will close the process once we have found the right candidate.

Apply now and join our team!

Ready for your next step? Click on ‘Apply now’ to get started right away! As long as the position is advertised, you can apply at any time.

We value diversity and therefore welcome all applicants - regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion/belief, disability, age, sexual orientation and identity, and any other protected status. You can find out more about our culture here Culture at Körber - it's worth taking a look!

If you have any questions or technical problems, please send us an e-mail to jobs@koerber.com. Mette Maria Holmegaard Nielsen is the responsible person for this job advertisement. We work with permanent partners and therefore ask recruitment consultants to refrain from contacting us by e-mail or telephone.

At Körber, we think long term and pursue objectives that apply across all of our business areas. In line with our vision of “Market Leadership through Technology Leadership,” we have defined our “Life 2035” goals for the next decade to ensure that Körber becomes the leading partner in our industries—Life Science, Supply Chain, and High-Tech Manufacturing—by 2035.Life 2035 is built on four pillars that define how we embrace our shaping role: Leadership, Innovation, Findependence, and Empowerment. Sustainably profitable growth and financial independence form the foundation for achieving our ambitious financial targets for the next decade. By 2035, we aim to achieve global revenues of €10 billion. You can find more at https://www.koerber.com/en/about-us/what-drives-us

Körber is a global technology company for intelligent manufacturing and supply chain solutions. As a reliable innovation partner, Körber turns entrepreneurial thinking into customer success by providing leading technology to fuel what’s next – from end-to-end pharma production and advanced supply chain solutions to high-tech machinery and process equipment. Körber combines deep domain expertise with integrated hardware, software, and digital services, to help customers take the next step.

For our client, world leader within sonar technology – Teledyne RESON A/S, we are looking for a Toolmaker, Machinist, or other background as a skilled operator of machine tools.

Company Profile:

Teledyne Marine is a world leader in supplying high-quality underwater acoustic solutions, underwater autonomous vehicles, navigation systems and software with global presence and service facilities around the world. In Teledyne Marine, Europe we are specialized in design, development, manufacturing, marketing and commissioning of advanced Multibeam sonar systems, Inertial Navigation Systems with Fiber Optic Gyro’s and sensor software for real-time data collection and processing. We operate in the hydrographic, offshore, dredging, defense & security and marine research business areas.

Job Summary:

As Teledyne RESON’s new Toolmaker, you will be part of the Technology and Products department. The group cooperates in defining, developing, testing, prepare production setup and handover of new products to Operations for numerous product lines.

Our products consist of real-time Single- and Multi-beam Sonar Systems, Inertial Navigation System and related products. Key parts are advanced sensors (Acoustical, Fiber Optic Gyro), low noise analog electronics, high power transmit stages and high performance signal processing platforms. The product lines span from small low power products for autonomous vehicle drones (ASV/AUV) to high-end deepwater sonar systems for large research vessels.

You will be working in the mechanical team with focus be on transducer prototyping, manufacturing processes, automation, and production support for new and existing products. You will be working with our current R&D workshop wizard who is retiring within 1 – 2 years. You will eventually be responsible for our R&D workshop. You will be part of development projects with design for manufacturability reviews, production tooling, procurement and set to work of production machines, prototyping build and documentation.

Key responsibilities:

• Prototype assembly of small- and full-scale acoustic sensors working close with the transducer designer

• Design and production of jigs, fixtures, dies, molds, machine- and cutting tools for prototype manufacturing.

• Material knowledge with metal, glue, plastic and urethane materials

• Build knowledge on glueing, priming and potting methods of various materials and metals

• Design for Manufacturing review (DFM)

• Support and maintenance of production equipment.

• Support to the daily operational tasks incl. troubleshooting and NCR/MRB-handling

• Corrective And Preventive Action (CAPA)

• Production documentation support to assembly- and test procedures

Job Requirements:

• Experience with setup and operation of lathes, milling machines, grinding machines, and jig grinders

• Experience with glueing, molding, potting of various materials is preferred

• Experience with CAD software is preferred.

• You are structured, systematic and quality-minded

• Drive and ability to complete task to agreed deadline

• Enjoy working both independently and in teams

• Proactive, positive and supporting personality

Educational level:

You have an education as a Toolmaker, Machinist, or other background as a skilled operator of machine tools.

Language skills:

Fluent in English to a professional level

Other relevant Information:

• Job position is in Slangerup, Denmark

If you want to know more, please contact:

HEGSØ Search & Consulting, chief consultant Anders Hegelskov, Phone: +45 3035 6405 – Mail: ah@hegsoe.dk

The Impact You'll Make

Danfoss is proud to be at the forefront of driving a global transformation in digital and electric solutions that increase productivity and energy efficiency.  We are truly passionate about investment, and innovation, as we continue to support our customers' journey towards a greener and lower-carbon future. We now have an exciting new oppourtunity to recruit a Cost-down Pipeline and ESG Manager, to be based from our headquarters in **Nordborg, Denmark.

**

This a high-visibility and high-impact global position, working at the intersection of procurement, engineering, and ESG, will offer you the scope to directly impact both our financial performance and carbon footprint, and help shape both cost transformation and sustainability agenda.  You'll lead a critical global agenda across our Controls division (~€450M spend), combining cost transformation, supplier strategy, and decarbonization, placing you at the center of value creation and sustainability.  You will have scope to drive a structured, high-impact cost-down pipeline while embedding ESG principles—especially Scope 3 emissions reduction—into sourcing decisions and supplier collaboration.

What You’ll Be Doing

In this role, you'll take ownership of:

• Delivering 3–4% annual cost reduction pipeline across a €450M global spend through a balanced, data‑driven cost‑down strategy

• Leading, coaching, and developing a global team of 3 Pipeline Project Managers to build strong capabilities and disciplined execution

• Standardize and strengthen cost‑down processes, tools, and governance, driving alignment across Category Management, Engineering, Operations, and other functions

• Embed ESG and decarbonization into sourcing by integrating CO₂ performance, monitoring Scope 3.1 impacts, and scaling low‑carbon cost‑reduction opportunities

• Drive supplier engagement and accountability to build and deliver a robust pipeline of decarbonization and cost‑down initiatives

What We're Looking For

• Strong experience in strategic procurement, cost-down, or value engineering, alongside a proven track record delivering measurable cost savings at scale

• Experience working cross-functionally with engineering and operations

• Leadership experience, with ability to drive performance through others

• Solid understanding of ESG, sustainability, or decarbonization in supply chains

• Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills in a global environment

• Analytical and structured mindset, with a hands-on execution approach.

Preferable would be:

Experience with Scope 3 emissions management

Background in industrial / manufacturing environments

What You'll Get from Us

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

Our Commitment to Transparency

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Brand

Danfoss engineers solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.

Our solutions are used in areas such as refrigeration, air conditioning, heating, power conversion, motor control, industrial machinery, marine, and on- and off-highway equipment. We also provide solutions for data centers, renewable energy, energy storage, heat recovery, as well as contribute to district energy solutions for cities.

Our innovative engineering dates back to 1933. Danfoss is family-owned and employs over 39,000 people. We create long-term value for our customers in more than 100 countries with a global footprint of around 100 factories.

The Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies (AIAS) is pleased to announce an exclusive fellowship opportunity for a researcher who holds a position at a Swedish research institution. The fellowship is made possible through a collaboration with Riksbankens Jubileumsfond in Sweden.The purpose of the AIAS-RJ fellowship is to strengthen the ties and expand collaborations between the Swedish and Danish research communities.

Why apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

AIAS is a haven for intellectual exploration, hosting excellent researchers eager to develop their work in an interdisciplinary, international and collaborative environment. AIAS nurtures an innovative atmosphere where breakthroughs emerge through transparent, inclusive and reflective discussions, offering a space for engagement and creativity.

The AIAS-RJ fellowship gives the selected fellow the opportunity to concentrate on their own research interests while also being an active member of the AIAS research community and participating in and contributing to seminars and activities beyond their own field of expertise. The fellow must be eager to engage in the interdisciplinary community at AIAS and expand research collaborations with colleagues at Aarhus University.

Who can apply for an AIAS-RJ Fellowship

The call is open to curiosity-driven researchers who:

• are of any nationality who hold a tenured position at a Swedish research institution

• work within the humanities and social sciences

• have a research experience of minimum 4 years after completion of the PhD

A unique interdisciplinary platform at AIAS

AIAS fosters connections, sparks ideas and dissolves boundaries as fellows engage with researchers from different disciplines within the Institute and across departments and research hubs at Aarhus University. Therefore, the call welcomes applications from all research areas and themes.

With a location within the unique campus of Aarhus University, AIAS functions as an interdisciplinary platform that connects researchers across Aarhus University and international scholars. AIAS has fellows who work in thematic groups or in individual fellowships, and hosts events and activities, which AIAS-RJ fellows are welcome to join and contribute to.

AIAS and Aarhus University strive to create a multidisciplinary, inclusive academic environment and to be an inspiring workplace for all by fostering a culture in which the individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The fellowship includes

The AIAS-RJ Fellow is offered:

• a salary based on seniority (employment conditions and wages are regulated through the Danish collective union agreements)

• travel costs to and from Aarhus

• relocation assistance

• a moderate budget for research-related costs

The AIAS-RJ Fellow will have office space at AIAS and can participate in academic training activities, conferences and workshops at AIAS. They will also be affiliated with the relevant research environments at Aarhus University.

How to apply: Application process and deadline

Applications must be submitted online via the system: GrantOne.

In the ‘Guide for Applicants,’ you can find the detailed application requirements and more information on the structure of the application system, the selection criteria and the selection process.

Timeline of the application process

• Opening of call: August 2026.

• Deadline for applications: 24 November 2026 at 12.00 (noon) CET.

• Evaluation and selection period: December 2026 - March 2027.

• Applicants will receive answers: Ultimo March 2027.

• Fellowship begins: 1 September 2027.

About AIAS

As an 'Institute for Advanced Study,' AIAS brings researchers together across disciplines, seniority and nationality. AIAS offers fellowships for excellent researchers from all academic disciplines to pursue cutting-edge research projects for the benefit of society and humankind in optimal research conditions.

The daily encounter with colleagues from diverse research disciplines at AIAS provides fellows with fresh and different insights, methods and perspectives on their own research, leading to new and unexpected research questions and ideas.

Data Governance Specialist

Are you keen to support an organization that's on an exciting data journey? Then come join TDC Brands.

As the Data Governance Specialist, you will be a member of the Data Office, responsible for supporting and developing data governance initiatives across the organization. In this role you will work flexibly between the Data Office and embedded in business units to make data roles work day-to-day: enabling data consumers, assisting Data Domain Owners and Data Stewards.

You will have an important role in supporting data governance by working collaboratively with the business.

Key Responsibilities:

Enable Data Consumers:

• Support adoption of the strategic data platform and the Enterprise Business Glossary (EBG) among data consumers in your business domain, including AI and agentic consumers.

• Help consumers find, understand, and trust governed data so it actually gets used for business insights and automation.

Assist Data Domain Owners:

• Support your Data Domain Owner(s) in maturing the data domain map and semantic models.

• Align with Tech, DPO and Legal as needed when data domain priorities, critical data elements, or AI classifications are being set.

• Flag gaps early — missing owners, unclear sources, unresolved dependencies — so each wave starts on solid ground.

Assist Data Stewards:

• Provide on-demand support to Data Stewards as they assess and authorize changes and stay accountable for data quality at source.

Stakeholder Engagement and Communication:

• Act as the day-to-day point of contact for Data Domain Owners, Data Stewards, Glossary Term Owners and data consumers.

• Escalate issues that need central Data Office, Tech, DPO or Legal involvement.

Bonus

Experience with telecoms, familiarity with data cataloging tools, or an interest in how governed data enables AI and agentic use cases.

Qualifications

As a Data Governance Specialist, we expect you to have sufficient years' experience in data management and data governance. You most likely come from an industry that prioritizes critical and valuable data assets and applies 'just enough' data governance.

Key expectations of the role are having great communication skills, comfort in operating pragmatically ahead of a fully defined policy landscape, and an ability to interact with people across the organization to produce tangible benefits to our data and AI initiatives.

Application: It is not necessary to attach a cover letter, but please include a brief introduction in your CV about why you are applying for this position. To ensure a fair and inclusive recruitment process, we kindly ask you to refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

Application date: 30/11/2026

We’re looking for a senior full-stack engineer with a strong interest in building AI-first products who enjoys owning problems end-to-end – from vague client needs and early hypotheses to production-grade systems that actually get used.

What you’ll do

You’ll join The Tech Collective (our Data & AI hub, specifically), where we help organisations design, build, and operationalise data- and AI-driven solutions.

This role is tailor-made for a systems thinker and builder – someone who has shipped real products, taken responsibility for technical direction, and is motivated by creating pragmatic solutions that combine data, software, and AI.

You’ll work closely with experienced AI specialists who bring deep model and ML expertise, while you focus on building robust products and software around those capabilities.

Your responsibilities will include:

• End-to-end solution ownership: designing and implementing full-stack applications from early concepts and prototypes to scalable, production-grade systems, including architecture decisions across frontend, backend, data, and cloud

• Modern full-stack development: building high-quality frontend and backend services, applying sound software engineering principles, and using AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully and critically

• AI-enabled product building: collaborating with AI specialists to integrate LLMs, retrieval pipelines, and agentic patterns into real products, and translating AI potential into solutions that make sense for organisations

• Data and systems thinking: designing data models, reasoning about distributed systems and trade-offs, and implementing event-driven or real-time features where they add value

• Observability and evaluation: experience setting up the right observability and eval tooling to establish traceability and iteratively improve on products

• Cloud, delivery, and collaboration: deploying and operating solutions in cloud environments, balancing speed, robustness, and security, and working closely with clients and stakeholders to create tangible business impact

What you’ll bring

We’re looking for someone with an AI builder mentality and 5+ years of hands-on full-stack experience, who is comfortable owning applications end to end – from frontend and backend to data and deployment.

You don’t need to tick every box, but you should recognise yourself in most of the following:

• Strong full-stack foundation: solid skills in TypeScript and/or Python, with experience building and shipping production systems

• Mentoring experience: helping other developers through technical sparring and code reviews

• Outward curiosity: actively seeking to understand client problems in detail and working in close collaboration with them to solve them

• Ownership and leadership: a track record of building substantial solutions from scratch (e.g., startup, scale-up, or personal ventures), taking responsibility for outcomes, and leading technical direction without relying on formal authority

• System-level thinking: the ability to reason about architecture, data flows, trade-offs, and failure modes across the stack, and to make pragmatic decisions in ambiguous contexts

• Critical technical judgement: a keen eye for identifying weaknesses in existing architectures and tech stacks, and knowing where and how to improve them

• Communication and collaboration: the ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders, work across disciplines, and learn from – and share knowledge with – others in the team and across Implement

• Tool agnostic: capable of choosing the right tool for the job

What we offer

We offer a role with technical ownership and influence, working in a 20-person team that feels much closer to a nerdy startup than a large corporation – while being firmly backed by Implement Consulting Group.

You’ll gain exposure to a wide range of data- and AI-driven problems across industries, all within a culture built on trust, curiosity, humility, resilience, and impact. You’ll also have great freedom to shape your own role, deepen your expertise, and grow in exactly the direction that motivates you.

Ready to shape the digital future with us? Apply ASAP.

About The Tech Collective

The Tech Collective is a fast-growing consulting company powered by Implement Consulting Group. We aim to make a positive difference in the consulting industry, believing that the ability to create change with impact and purpose is a prerequisite for success in a global and turbulent world.

We’re expanding our team and look forward to meeting talented people who are curious about a career in information systems and management consulting at the intersection of business and technology.

Design products for athletes around the world that translate the data from Trackman’s best-in-class radar technology into actionable insights that help our users build a better game.

You’ll be joining our team of ~20 product designers from Canada, Mexico, Australia, England, Latvia, New Zealand, Slovakia, Ireland, and Denmark who have fun and challenge each other every day in delivering exceptional design work.

About the role

We're looking for a Product Designer to join our team. You'll work closely with designers, developers, and product owners on experiences, owning specific areas of the user journey over time. You will:

• 
Turn complex performance data into interfaces that are simply enjoyable to use, from social sessions with friends to immersive training and entertainment setups.

• 
Conduct user research, validate ideas, and deliver pixel-perfect designs.

• 
Collaborate closely with your developers and product owner in a dedicated product team.

Figma recently featured our team in a customer story on how we built a design-first culture at Trackman. Worth a read before you apply:

How Trackman built a design-first culture and a competitive edge

Job requirements

• 
4+ years of product design experience on a dedicated product team (university projects don't count).

• 
Strong visual communication and UI design skills. You can turn complex information into clear, intuitive interfaces, and work confidently within design systems.

• 
Clear, confident communication. You can explain your decision-making and are flexible when provided with feedback.

• 
Comfort with ambiguity and changing priorities.

• 
A portfolio that shows real problems, real constraints, and real outcomes.

Bonus points for

• 
Interest in sports, performance or entertainment products.

• 
Experience running or contributing to user research, and turning insights into design decisions.

• 
Experience with data-heavy products or visualizing performance data.

What you get

• 
A design team that genuinely love working together and helping each other grow through regular critiques, feedback sessions, and plenty of informal sparring.

• 
Access to our onsite fitness center, all-you-can-play golf simulator, a great lunch and much more!

• 
Social happenings and company events throughout the year.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These therapies are designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage, with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Medical Writing, you will be dedicated to one of our compounds under clinical development, taking ownership of the clinical and regulatory writing that helps move this compound through development. You will turn complex clinical and scientific evidence into clear, accurate documents that regulators can act on - connecting the science, data and development strategy into one coherent story.

This is a hands-on role. You will write, shape and drive documents yourself while bringing physicians, scientists, biostatisticians and regulatory colleagues together around high-quality outputs and demanding timelines.

What You'll Do At Hemab

• Own medical writing for one of our leading compounds, from document strategy and planning through drafting, review and finalization.

• Lead development of clinical documents, including clinical study protocols, clinical study reports, Investigator’s Brochures, and clinical submission documents appropriate to the program’s stage.

• Contribute to clinical content of regulatory and safety documents, such as briefing documents, regulatory responses, and DSURs.

• Translate complex clinical and statistical data into clear, scientifically accurate narratives for regulatory reviewers.

• Partner closely with clinical development, regulatory, biostatistics, safety, and other scientific colleagues to align document content with the program strategy.

• Drive cross-functional document reviews, resolve comments constructively and build alignment without compromising scientific accuracy.

• Apply relevant regulatory requirements and guidance, including ICH E3, ICH E6 and applicable FDA and EMA expectations.

• Build writing plans and practical frameworks that keep interdependent documents moving against development and submission timelines.

• Maintain document quality, consistency and version control while adapting quickly as data, priorities and timelines evolve.

• Identify writing or documentation risks early, take ownership of solutions and give the program team a clear view of what is needed next.

• Collaborate with internal cross-functional teams and external vendors to manage public disclosure activities in compliance with transparency rules.

What You'll Bring to Hemab

Essential:

• Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific discipline, with at least 10 years of hands-on medical writing experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical or CRO clinical research environments.

• Significant experience authoring clinical and regulatory documents across drug development.

• Strong working knowledge of ICH E3, ICH E6 and relevant FDA and EMA requirements.

• Scientific fluency and the ability to interpret clinical trial data and statistical outputs accurately.

• Excellent written English, with the ability to make complex science clear, structured and precise.

• Strong cross-functional communication skills and experience bringing multiple expert reviewers to alignment.

• Ability to own competing documents and deadlines independently while maintaining quality.

Nice to have

• Advanced scientific degree such as an MS, PhD or PharmD.

• Medical writing certification or relevant regulatory affairs training.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. You'll create some of the writing frameworks you need rather than inherit a finished system. We work across Copenhagen and Cambridge and priorities can move quickly as clinical data and development plans change.

You'll need to solve problems when you reach the first wall rather than pass them on. That means taking ownership, asking for help when you need it, working without ego and being comfortable making progress when every answer isn't available yet. At a company our size, how you work matters as much as pedigree. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the work, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

Your writing will sit close to the point where clinical science becomes a potential treatment for patients. People living with serious bleeding disorders have spent too long reacting to bleeds after they happen. We're working to give them the chance to prevent them.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty and respect. We want the same from our hiring experience - transparent, human and clear from first conversation to final answer.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. Reasonable adjustments are available at any stage of the hiring experience.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

In Danish:

The Department of Accounting invites applications for a PhD position in Auditing. The Department of Accounting is one of the oldest and largest accounting departments in Europe. We have a growing and flourishing research environment within financial accounting, management accounting and control, auditing, and corporate governance.

We especially welcome PhD proposals that adopt qualitative research methods and suggest novel approaches to the study of

• The making of the audit profession, especially regarding emerging technologies in auditing, such as generative artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on how they may reshape the audit profession, including the training and socialization of auditors, the exercise of professional judgment and the relevance of the traditional audit model in responding to evolving societal demands.
• Audit firm ownership, including the emerging role of private equity firms acquiring ownership interests in audit firms. Proposals within this research theme may explore implications for, for example, the partnership model, audit firm governance, how audits are conducted, talent management, client portfolios, audit market competition, and how these developments may reconfigure the audit profession.
• The role of auditing and assurance in sustainable development. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to explore alternative forms of auditing and assurance that contribute to sustainable development and to propose empirical work that goes beyond simply examining the current compliance-oriented role associated with the verification of sustainability reports. Proposals should aim to develop research that provides a basis for debate about how auditing and assurance can play a meaningful role in sustainability.
• Regulator-auditor interaction, with a focus on challenges and potential pathways in public oversight practices, including, for example, the role of firm-level oversight practices and dialogue, as well as the role of ad hoc regulatory investigations alongside routine quality inspections.
• Client-auditor interaction, with a focus on, for example, the governance role of audit committees, the negotiation of accounting issues, professional and commercial conflicts, or the role of client technology adoption in the performance of audits.
• Auditing in the context of audit firm organization and governance, with the aim of understanding how increasingly intensive and sophisticated audit firm-level systems (e.g., quality management, incentive systems, performance measurement, and culture/tone at the top) operate to manage and control auditor behavior within audit firms. Within this theme, candidates are encouraged to propose research that can inform reflections on how bureaucracy in audit firms can be balanced, how tendencies toward defensive behavior might be reversed, and how professional judgment at all levels, from junior auditors to partners, might be encouraged.
The project should speak to contemporary concerns in auditing and aim to contribute to academic, public, professional, and company-level debates. The PhD project should therefore be informed and enriched by engagement with firms and professionals as part of both the research process and the dissemination of research findings, and we encourage proposals to demonstrate the potential for such engagement.

The PhD position is based in the Department of Accounting, and the candidate will be part of the department’s auditing research group. We welcome applicants with degrees or experience in accounting and auditing. We also welcome applicants from other social sciences who are interested in engaging with auditing as a research domain. The auditing research group consists of researchers with backgrounds in accounting and auditing, as well as researchers from other academic fields who have a strong interest in auditing. The PhD candidate will work in close collaboration with the supervisors and benefit from the international research environment in the Department of Accounting and at CBS. Candidates are encouraged to contact Professor Thomas Riise Johansen (trj.acc@cbs.dk) for informal discussions and information about the position before submitting the application.

About the PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant will show an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/acc

Application and admission requirements
The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must:

• have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)
• have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale (https://ufm.dk/en/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system)
• have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted. In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.
• have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS
• master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking
The application (see link below) must include a five-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed empirical material
• a work plan for the three years
More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmemes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts
• documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met)
• a concise curriculum vitae (CV)
• a list of articles and publications (if applicable)
• one example of a selected written work (e.g. master's thesis)
The PhD student is enrolled in the CBS PhD School. Further information about PhD scholarships and the PhD programme can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmeme.Information about the department can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/forskning/institutter-centre/institut-regnskab.

For additional information regarding the PhD position, feel free to contact Professor, Thomas Riise Johansen, trj.acc@cbs.dk.

Employment and salary
A PhD scholarship runs for a period of three years and includes teaching obligations corresponding to 416 work hours. The scholarships are fully salaried positions, according to the national Danish collective agreement. The monthly salary is currently approximately DKK 30,264 up to DKK 36,877 depending on seniority and a pension contribution totaling 18.07%. The scholarship includes tuition fees, office space, course and travel costs (according to the current CBS agreement). 

Salary level and employment take place in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's agreement with the Academics' Central Organization.

Recruitment procedure 
The Recruitment Committee shortlists at least two-five applicants to be assessed by the Assessment Committee. Applicants are informed whether their application has proceeded for assessment.

Applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and will receive their personal assessment later. Selected applicants will be invited for an interview. Please note that a positive assessment does not automatically result in an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application. 

The application must be sent via the online link below. 
Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see above), by the application deadline.

Details about Copenhagen Business School are available at www.cbs.dk/en.

Apply for position

WE TRANSFORM SOCIETY WITH BUSINESS

CBS is a globally recognised business school with deep roots in the Nordic socio-economic model. Our faculty has a broad focus on societal challenges, and we have earned a reputation for high-quality disciplinary and interdisciplinary research and education.
We are located at Frederiksberg and have approximately 20,000 full and part-time students, 800 full-time faculty members, 200 PhD students and 700 administrative staff, and a full portfolio of bachelor, master, MBA/EMBA, PhD and executive programmes taught in English and Danish.
Our global profile carries the obligation to address critical challenges in our research and to develop the transformational capabilities of students, graduates and business leaders via our educational activities and opportunities for lifelong learning. Complex challenges call for joint action, and therefore our strategy focuses on strengthening current and starting new partnerships with other sciences, the business community, authorities and civil society.
CBS is working continuously on becoming a diverse and inclusive organisation, and we encourage all regardless of gender identity and expression, ethnicity, religious beliefs, LGBT+ identity, cultural background etc. to apply.Reach out to us if you need assistance in the application or recruitment process, if there is something we should know, or if as a person with disability you wish to make use of your preferential access.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in the intellectual history of corporate politics at CBS
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a vacant PhD scholarship within the field of the intellectual history of coporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. Expected starting date is 1 May 2027.

The PhD position is a non-tenured full-time position of 3 years, with teaching and course work obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The PhD project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk).

About Department of Business Humanities and Law (BHL) at CBS
Department of Business Humanities and Law explores how people, organisations, institutions, and societies shape business. Its core research themes include entrepreneurship, business ethics, leadership, governance, culture, learning, business history, and business law from commercial and societal perspectives. The department comprises three academic units and nine reseach groups.

Teaching responsibilities of the Department include undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programmes are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within BHL the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society.

PhD programme
The three-year PhD programme at CBS gives you the opportunity to conduct research under the supervision of CBS’s associate professors and professors, supported by research related PhD courses. The programme is highly international, and you are expected to participate in international research conferences and to spend time at another research institution as a visiting PhD student. See the CBS homepage for more information about the PhD programme, https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programme. 

CBS PhD graduates are held in high esteem not only in academia and research institutions but also in government and business where their research qualifications are in high demand.

CBS is committed to ensuring excellence, transformative and relevant teaching and research. Candidates who wish to join us must be interested in working in an organisation of this type and it is expected that the applicant shows an interest in joining the department's research environment. You can read more about the department's research here: www.cbs.dk/bhl.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a master’s degree in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy.

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
Application and admission requirements

The department will give priority to applicants with high grades from their universities. To be considered the applicant must

• have a basic education at master's level (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process)
• have received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master's thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale(https://ufsn.dk/english/education/the-danish-education-system/grading-system/) 
• have a weighted grade point average of at least 8.2 on the Danish 7-point grading scale for the bachelor's and master's degree combined or alternatively a weighted grade point average must be at least 9.5 for the master's degree alone. If the grade point average is not met, documentation for being in the top 40% of the class is also accepted.
• have completed the master's programme before starting the PhD programme at CBS
• master academic English at a high level in writing and speaking
The application (see link below) must include a five-page PhD project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed empirical material
• a work plan for the three years
More information can be found here: https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programmes/admission

In addition to the project description, copies of the following must be included:

• motivation cover letter
• diploma for bachelor's and master's degree or other certificates at an equivalent level as well as the grade transcripts
• documentation for being in the top 40% of the class (if grade requirements are not met). In rare cases, the grade requirement can be waived.
• a concise curriculum vitae (CV)
• a list of articles and publications (if applicable)
• one example of a selected written work (e.g. master's thesis)
• documentation of English language skills is not required for the application but may be requested if the applicant is shortlisted for interviews.
The PhD student is enrolled in the CBS PhD School. Further information about PhD scholarships and the PhD programme can be found at https://www.cbs.dk/en/research/phd-programme.

For further information please contact Associate Professor Mathias Hein-Jessen, email mhj.bhl@cbs.dk or Head of Department Pia Bramming, email pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department can be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl

Employment and salary
A PhD scholarship runs for a period of three years and includes teaching obligations corresponding to 416 work hours. The scholarships are fully salaried positions, according to the national Danish collective agreement. The monthly salary is currently approximately DKK 30,264 up to DKK 36,877 depending on seniority and a pension contribution totalling 18,07 %. The scholarship includes tuition fees, office space, course and travel costs (according to the current CBS agreement). 

Salary level and employment take place in accordance with the Ministry of Finance's agreement with the Academics' Central Organization.

Recruitment procedure 

The Recruitment Committee comprised of tenured faculty shortlists at least two-five applicants to be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline.

Applicants shortlisted for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and will receive the result of their personal assessment later. When the assessment committee has finished their work selected applicants will be invited for an interview. Please note that a positive assessment does not automatically result in an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application. 

The application must be sent via the electronic recruitment system. 

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see above), by the application deadline.

Details about Copenhagen Business School are available at www.cbs.dk/en.

Application due 12/15/2026

Job Title: Business Operations Coordinator

Company: Kern Hansen Erhvervsrengøring

Location: Fjeldhammervej 15 2610 Rødovre 

Employment Type: Full-time (160 hours per month)

About the Company

Kern Hansen Erhvervsrengøring (CVR: 25479947) is an established(we are operating from 2000) and quality driven commercial cleaning company based in Rodovre. We pride ourselves on delivering premium, reliable cleaning and maintenance services to a wide portfolio of corporate clients across the region. To support our continuous growth and ensure our exceptionally high service standards, we are looking for a structured and energetic Business Operations Coordinator to join our operational team.

About the Role

We are seeking an organized, proactive, and detail oriented Business Operations Coordinator. In this pivotal role, you will serve as the central link between our office, our valued client accounts, and our dedicated field teams. You will drive operational efficiency, ensure high-quality service delivery, and lead our field staff to success on a daily basis.

Key Responsibilities

* Operational Scheduling: Oversee and manage weekly and monthly staff shift scheduling to ensure optimal workforce distribution across all client locations.

* Quality Assurance Audits: Conduct systematic on-site inspections using established company checklists to guarantee that service delivery consistently meets our strict contractual standards.

* Team Leadership & Support: Act as the primary operational point of contact for field staff, effectively resolving daily issues and fostering collaborative teamwork.

* Performance Metrics & Reporting: Maintain meticulous records of team attendance, monitor job completion timelines, and report operational progress to management.

* Account Coordination: Manage client relationships, review service evaluation data, and maintain all corporate account and contract documentation.

Qualifications & Requirements

* Education: A relevant Bachelor’s degree (e.g., Business Management, Business Administration, or similar commercial fields).

* Skills: Strong organizational, planning, and interpersonal communication skills with a problem-solving mindset.

* Language: Fluency in professional English (both written and spoken) is required.

* IT Literacy: Solid proficiency in everyday computer tools, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and dedicated digital scheduling systems.

What We Offer

* A full-time position (160 hours per month ) in a dynamic, supportive work environment.

* A competitive salary package corresponding to Danish labor market standards.

How to Apply

Please send your CV and application to Kern@kernhansen.dk 

We review applications on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: Executive and Management Secretary Wanted for T&M ApS
jobs.description:
T&M ApS is a company with restaurants and stores. We are looking for an experienced and independent secretary to assist our management in a central and versatile role.

About the position

As an Executive and Management Secretary, you will be a close sparring partner for management and will be responsible for a broad range of tasks. You will handle everything from calendar management and meeting preparation to correspondence, documentation and coordination across our business areas.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Administrative support for the executive management and leadership

• 
Calendar management, meeting invitations and minute-taking

• 
Preparation and handling of correspondence and documents

• 
Coordination between restaurants and stores

• 
Preparation of presentations, reports and other management materials

• 
Other administrative tasks as required

We expect you to:

• 
Have a relevant business management education

• 
Be structured, detail-oriented and able to work independently

• 
Have strong communication skills in English

• 
Be able to handle multiple tasks simultaneously in a busy working environment

We offer:

• 
An exciting and versatile position in a company in development

• 
Close cooperation with management and good opportunities for development

• 
An informal and committed working environment

• 
Salary according to qualifications

We look forward to hearing from you!
